identification.summary: Storm-0302 is Microsoft's name for a financially motivated eCrime actor that CrowdStrike tracks as NARWHAL SPIDER and Proofpoint as TA544; BlueVoyant uses all three names for the same activity [S1][S3][S5]. CrowdStrike describes NARWHAL SPIDER as the criminal actor that developed and operated the Cutwail version 2 spam engine, which dates to 2007 and is delivered through the Pushdo loader [S3]. Proofpoint describes TA544 as a highly financially motivated actor distributing Ursnif and URLZone against Italy, western Europe and Japan [S2]. Proofpoint also tied TA544 to the WikiLoader downloader, first seen December 2022 [S6].
identification.firstObserved: Proofpoint began tracking TA544 in February 2017 [S2]. CrowdStrike dates the Cutwail spam engine to 2007, but that is the malware's history, not necessarily this actor's [S3].
identification.notes: Name mapping per Microsoft is in the record's existing MS source; BlueVoyant independently equates Narwhal Spider, Storm-0302 and TA544 [S5]. The actor's relationship to the Cutwail botnet (spam-for-hire) means campaign payloads may belong to customers rather than the actor; do not merge customer malware families into this cluster [S3]. WikiLoader was also distributed by a second actor, TA551, which is a separate Proofpoint cluster [S6].

attribution.sponsor: Criminal (non-state). No state sponsor is stated in the cited sources.
attribution.confidence: Vendor-level only. Name equivalence is stated by BlueVoyant and Microsoft's naming table; the NaurLegal campaign link is BlueVoyant's own belief [S5]. No government attribution found.
attribution.basis: CrowdStrike lists the Russian Federation as the actor's location [S3]. BlueVoyant attributed the March 2024 NaurLegal campaign to Narwhal Spider (Storm-0302, TA544) based on WikiLoader-linked infrastructure [S5][S7]. Proofpoint tied WikiLoader's first campaign to TA544 [S6].

objectives: Financial gain: distributing banking trojans and loaders via mass phishing and spam [S2][S3]. CrowdStrike states Cutwail campaign targets and payloads are determined by NARWHAL SPIDER's customers, i.e. spam is sold as a service [S3].

sectors: Financial services and general commercial recipients (banking-trojan targets)
Professional and legal services customers (NaurLegal lure)
targeting.notes: Proofpoint says TA544 focuses on Italy and Japan [S2]. CrowdStrike saw a Japanese-language campaign starting 24 October 2018 that fetched URLZone only when the system language was Japanese [S4]. Proofpoint reported a 2021 surge of Ursnif campaigns against Italian organizations using courier and energy-company lures and geofencing [S8]. BlueVoyant reported the group expanding beyond Italy toward the end of 2023, and the 7 March 2024 wave reached Canada and Europe [S5][S7]. Sector targeting is opportunistic; no specific military or government targeting is stated in the sources.

capabilities.summary: Operates the Cutwail v2 spam engine, delivered through the Pushdo loader, and sells spam services to other criminals including TrickBot developers and operators of URLZone, Nymaim and Gozi ISFB [S3]. TA544 delivery has used Office attachments with malicious macros, steganography in embedded images, and geofencing to check recipient location before infection [S2][S8]. In October 2018 CrowdStrike observed malicious PowerShell combined with steganography to deliver URLZone [S4]. WikiLoader is a downloader that checks connectivity by requesting Wikipedia and looking for the string 'The Free'; Proofpoint counted at least eight campaigns since December 2022, with Excel/VBA, OneNote and PDF lures, and Ursnif as the usual payload [S6]. Proofpoint judged WikiLoader may be rented to other criminals [S6]. In March 2024 BlueVoyant reported PDF invoices impersonating law firms, with command and control via compromised WordPress sites and VirusTotal hints of IcedID as a payload [S5][S7].

campaigns.name: Panda Banker email campaigns against Italy
campaigns.summary: Proofpoint began tracking TA544 when email campaigns against Italian customers using Panda Banker were reported [S2].

campaigns.name: Japanese-language Cutwail campaign delivering URLZone
campaigns.summary: From 24 October 2018 CrowdStrike observed Cutwail spam using malicious PowerShell and steganography to deliver URLZone (Bebloh), conditional on a Japanese system language. The final payload was not observed and CrowdStrike noted spam levels had been lower in the prior three months [S4].

campaigns.name: Ursnif surge against Italy
campaigns.summary: Proofpoint reported that Ursnif campaigns against Italy from January to August 2021 exceeded the 2020 total, using courier and energy-company payment lures and geofencing [S8].

campaigns.name: WikiLoader first campaign
campaigns.summary: On 27 December 2022 the first WikiLoader version appeared in a campaign spoofing the Italian Revenue Agency, attributed by Proofpoint to TA544 [S6].

campaigns.name: NaurLegal law-firm invoice phishing
campaigns.summary: BlueVoyant named and attributed to Narwhal Spider a 7 March 2024 wave of PDFs posing as law-firm invoices, reaching Italy, Canada and Europe, with WikiLoader-linked infrastructure on compromised WordPress sites [S5][S7].

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated eCrime operator tracked as Storm-0302 / NARWHAL SPIDER / TA544; CrowdStrike lists Russia as location [S3][S5].
diamond.capability: Cutwail v2 spam engine and Pushdo loader; WikiLoader; macro, PowerShell and steganography delivery; customer payloads such as URLZone, Ursnif, Gozi ISFB [S2][S3][S4][S6].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised WordPress sites used for command and control in NaurLegal, with domains linked to WikiLoader [S5][S7]. Cutwail botnet of infected hosts [S3].
diamond.victim: Organizations and individuals in Italy and Japan, expanding to Canada, Europe and potentially the US [S2][S5][S7].
diamond.socioPolitical: Criminal profit motive; no political objective stated in sources [S2][S3].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints and email clients; Office macros, PDF, OneNote lures; PowerShell [S4][S6][S7].

gaps: Microsoft's own reporting on Storm-0302 was not found or opened; only the naming-table entry is known.
Activity after March 2024 was not found in searches; current status is unknown.
Direct fetches of BlueVoyant, Proofpoint and Malpedia pages failed (host resolution), so details rely on search-result summaries and secondary coverage.
The Proofpoint TA544 profile ('TA544 Buffet of Malware') and CrowdStrike adversary page were seen only as search summaries and are undated, so they are cited without a firm publication date.
Publication month of the Proofpoint WikiLoader post is not confirmed from the page; 2023-08 is an estimate to be verified.
Whether the Cutwail operation and WikiLoader/Ursnif activity are run by the same people, versus customers, is not established.
No indicators, CVE exploitation or victim counts verified; one database reportedly lists no attributed CVEs and another note mentions a Windows SmartScreen one-day, unverified.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: the actor is a criminal spam-for-hire and loader operator with no stated state tasking, so its relevance to defended networks is as a delivery channel for banking trojans and loaders (Ursnif, URLZone, IcedID possible) [S2][S3][S5]. Step 3-4: MLCOA is mass phishing with PDF, Office or OneNote lures that pull a WikiLoader-style downloader from compromised websites [S6][S7]. MDCOA is customer payloads of higher impact, as BlueVoyant noted IcedID could indicate more destructive follow-on [S5]. Candidate indicators: invoice-themed PDFs from law-firm names, WikiLoader's Wikipedia connectivity check with 'The Free' string, geofenced or language-gated payload retrieval, and compromised WordPress C2 [S4][S6][S7].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: track this cluster as an email-borne initial-access enabler and watch for expansion to US and Canadian targets [S5][S7]. Authorities: response is a defensive, network-owner action (blocking, email filtering, account reset); no offensive action is implied by the sources. Mission assurance: prioritize email gateway and endpoint controls for macro, PDF and OneNote attachments and monitor for loader-to-ransomware chains if customers change [S5][S6]. Coordination: share indicators through established vendor and law-enforcement channels; the sources give no government advisory.
